title: Determining the distribution of granule diameter from biological sludge
author: Alves, Del Nery, et al.
materials: -Image Pro-Plus Software (version 6.0);-HP Scanjet scanner 3770;-precision ruler;-calibrated spheres of different diameters: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 mm;-glue;-volumetric flask;-6 Petri dishes;-Plastic Pasteur pipette;-water;-MS Excel or similar program (for data acquisition and calculation).
N.B.: any scanner and image analysis software with similar characteristics can be used.

steps.title: Gather equipment and software
steps.instruction: Collect all required items: Image Pro‑Plus software (version 6.0), HP Scanjet 3770 (or any comparable scanner), precision ruler, calibrated steel spheres of 1 mm, 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm and 5 mm diameter, glue, volumetric flask, six Petri dishes, plastic Pasteur pipette, water, and MS Excel (or equivalent) for data handling.

steps.title: Perform benchmark calibration with steel spheres
steps.instruction: Run a benchmark test using the calibrated steel spheres (1–5 mm) to assess the accuracy and precision of the image‑analysis workflow before measuring actual granules.

steps.title: Evaluate sample volumes
steps.instruction: Test three sample volumes—5 mL, 10 mL and 15 mL—to determine the most suitable volume for the granulometry assay.

steps.title: Capture images of granule samples
steps.instruction: Place each Petri dish containing the granule suspension on the scanner and acquire a high‑resolution image using the HP Scanjet 3770 (or any equivalent scanner). Save the images in a format compatible with Image Pro‑Plus.

steps.title: Analyze images with Image Pro‑Plus
steps.instruction: Process each captured image in Image Pro‑Plus to obtain granule diameter measurements.

substeps.instruction: Open the first captured image in Image Pro‑Plus (v6.0).
Select “Measure” → “Calibration” → “Select Spatial” → choose “Spatial Cal 0” and click “Apply” (repeat for every new image).
Choose the “Ellipse” tool and carefully outline the Petri dish, avoiding the dish edge.
Open “Measurements”, click “Select Measurements”, then enable “Diameter Mean” (or any other desired measurement) and confirm with “OK”.
Click “Count” and verify that granules appear marked in red.
Choose “File” → “Clipboard” to copy the measurement values.
Paste the copied values into an Excel worksheet for later statistical analysis.
If the image contains multiple Petri dishes, repeat the ellipse outlining and measurement steps for each dish within the same image.
Proceed to the next image and repeat the entire procedure, starting again with the spatial calibration.
